query: For MnNiSi-based magnetic-refrigeration materials, what single intervention could improve mechanical performance while retaining a large magnetocaloric effect? Formulate one hypothesis that specifies the intervention, its proposed mechanism, the expected changes relative to an appropriate baseline, the conditions under which it should hold, supporting prior evidence, and an experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Doping MnNiSi-based magnetic-refrigeration materials with a small amount of boron (less than 1 at.%) will improve their mechanical performance by enhancing grain boundary cohesion, thereby increasing their compressive strength by at least 15% relative to the as-synthesized state, while retaining a large magnetocaloric effect, under operating conditions of 20-50°C and magnetic fields up to 2 Tesla.
generation.material_initial_state: as-synthesized or processed state with existing mechanical and magnetocaloric properties
generation.conditions: operating conditions for magnetic refrigeration, including temperature ranges of 20-50°C and magnetic fields up to 2 Tesla
generation.mechanism: enhanced grain boundary cohesion due to boron doping, leading to improved mechanical performance
generation.predicted_outcome: increase in compressive strength by at least 15%
generation.boundary: 20-50°C and magnetic fields up to 2 Tesla
generation.uncertainty: The actual effect of boron doping on the magnetocaloric effect is uncertain and may require further investigation to fully understand the trade-offs between mechanical performance and magnetocaloric properties.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare MnNiSi-based samples with and without boron doping (less than 1 at.%), measure their compressive strength and magnetocaloric effect under the specified operating conditions.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the boron-doped samples show a decrease in compressive strength or a significant reduction (more than 10%) in magnetocaloric effect compared to the undoped samples, the hypothesis is falsified.
